resolve.because: Billing publishes payment.<state> to fleet.workorder.events; both work-order's workorder.payment.audit queue and notification's notification.payment.events queue bind payment.# there, so both receive it.

The status host is a property no configuration of the set defines (billing's application.yml sets only the accounting lookup, legacy and SFTP addresses), and the region comes from an environment variable; nothing shows it is one of the internal units.

The outbox rows are written with the exchange fleet.workorder.events and the keys workorder.created, workorder.<id>.completed, workorder.<id>.cancelled and maintenance.reminder; notification-service binds all four, and work-order's own read-model queue binds workorder.created.

risks.reference: Workorder and billing both verify HMAC JWTs with the same secret placeholder under the internal profile; the secret
risks.how: Both services build an HMAC JWT decoder from the same shared-secret property, defaulted to a placeholder value in config.

risks.reference: The gateway composite calls `/api/technicians/{id}/skils`; technician-service serves `/api/technicians/{id}/skills`
risks.how: Gateway calls the misspelled /skils path while technician-service maps /skills.

risks.reference: The customer BFF requests technician availability without the serviceCode query parameter required by
risks.how: BFF calls availability with no query parameter while technician-service requires a serviceCode request parameter.

risks.reference: The work-order Feign client declares GET for `/api/technicians/{id}/shifts/{shiftId}/reschedule`, while
risks.how: Feign client uses GET for the reschedule path that technician-service maps only as POST.

risks.reference: PaymentService publishes RabbitMQ and JMS messages from a transactional method without a shared transactional outbox; a
risks.how: pay() is @Transactional and sends Rabbit and JMS messages before the transaction commits, with no outbox.

risks.reference: The shared permission aspect checks whether the forwarded role string contains the required role text; a longer role
risks.how: The aspect uses String.contains on the forwarded roles string, so a longer role value passes.

risks.reference: Work-order binds identity headers
risks.how: Work-order binds X-User-Id and X-Roles from the request with getHeader, which returns the first value, while the gateway adds (not replaces) those headers, so a client's own values win through the gateway too.

risks.reference: Billing declares Spring Boot 3.2.12 and uses the older `openjdk:17.0.2-jdk-slim` image; review support and security
risks.how: Billing pins Spring Boot 3.2.12 and an older openjdk 17.0.2 base image.

risks.reference: The Commons repository HEAD declares 2.3.0 while notification and work-order pin 1.9.4 and 2.1.0; both consumers are
risks.how: Notification pins commons 1.9.4 and work-order 2.1.0 (and parent 1.4.0-SNAPSHOT) while commons HEAD is 2.3.0.

risks.reference: The staff app calls GET /api/staff/operations/summary, while the gateway declares only customer and work-order route
risks.how: Staff app calls /staff/operations/summary but the gateway routes only /customer/** and /api/work-orders/**.

risks.reference: VehicleHistoryController and VehicleMaintenanceController declare the same GET /api/vehicles/{vin}/history handler
risks.how: Two controllers under /api/vehicles both map GET /{vin}/history.

risks.reference: Compose provides predictable local fallback credentials for databases and brokers
risks.how: Compose supplies predictable fallback passwords via ${VAR:-not-a-real-password}.

risks.reference: The production Helm infrastructure template declares one replica for each stateful workload; this does not provide an
risks.how: The infrastructure StatefulSet template hardcodes replicas: 1 for every stateful workload.

risks.reference: The export selects completed work orders by creation time within the last 24 hours, not completion time; a job
risks.how: The export filters completed orders by w.created_at over the last 86400 seconds, not by completion time.

risks.reference: Billing selects completed work-order rows and accepted estimates through a second JDBC connection to the workorder
risks.how: Billing opens a second datasource to the workorder database and selects from work_orders and estimates.

risks.reference: The payment audit queue has a listener, but its handler is empty and does not persist an audit record.
risks.how: The listener method body is empty, so nothing is recorded.

risks.reference: The work-order read-model listener splits a pipe-delimited string; the outbox publishes created events as structured
risks.how: Listener expects a pipe-delimited string while the poller publishes decoded JSON bodies.

risks.reference: The customer mutation requests BookingReceipt.workOrderId, which the BFF GraphQL schema does not expose; GraphQL
risks.how: The query selects workOrderId, which the BookingReceipt GraphQL type does not declare.

risks.reference: The staff STOMP client sets only a broker URL and does not explicitly provide a token
risks.how: STOMP client passes no token while the server rejects CONNECT/SUBSCRIBE without a user, so connection success is unproven.

risks.reference: The customer fetch and BFF work-order client do not explicitly attach a bearer token, while work-order creation
risks.how: Fetch sends no Authorization header and the BFF client adds none, while create requires the FLEET_CUSTOMER role.

risks.reference: No committed test sources exist for notification-service, edge-gateway, platform-config, platform-discovery,
risks.how: Absence: these units have no src/test folder (notification and edge-gateway contain only src/main); the cited pom shows notification opts out of JaCoCo.

risks.reference: The work-order and billing production profiles enable SQL bind TRACE logging; sensitive bound values may be written to logs.
risks.how: The work-order and billing prod profiles turn on TRACE logging of SQL and its bound values.

risks.reference: Notification-service marks four endpoints with the shared role annotation but neither imports nor scans the permission aspect that enforces it, so those role checks do not run.
risks.how: The endpoints carry @RequiresFleetRole, but the application neither imports PermissionAspect nor scans io.fleetcare.commons, so nothing enforces the annotation.

risks.reference: Billing declares only the work-order read DataSource as a bean, so Spring Boot does not create the billing DataSource its configuration describes; the billing JDBC client, Flyway and transactions would bind to the workorder database.
risks.how: The only DataSource bean points at the workorder database, so Boot's own DataSource backs off and billing's JDBC client, Flyway and transactions use that one.

risks.reference: PartnerStatusClient is a component that resolves `accounting.status-host` and `accounting.status-api-version` in its constructor; no configuration in the set defines them, so billing fails to start unless an outside source supplies them.
risks.how: The component's constructor needs two properties that no configuration file of the set defines, so the context fails to start without an outside value.

decoys.looksLike: Technician-service trusts role values for @PreAuthorize checks that might come from a request.
decoys.safeBecause: Roles are read from the realm_access claim of a JWT validated by oauth2ResourceServer and every exchange except health requires authentication; no identity header is read.

decoys.looksLike: Database passwords appear in service configuration, like a hardcoded secret.
decoys.safeBecause: They are bare environment placeholders with no default value, so no secret is in the code.

decoys.looksLike: Work-order service has JPA and a database but may let Hibernate manage the schema.
decoys.safeBecause: ddl-auto is validate and Flyway is enabled, so schema changes come only from migrations.
